questions.q: N,N-Dimethylethylamine N-oxide is heated. The products are:
questions.explain: The N-oxide oxygen removes a β-H as the C–N bond breaks, giving the alkene and (CH₃)₂N–OH. No external base is needed.

options: A syn (Ei) elimination through a five-membered cyclic transition state
An anti E2 elimination with an external base
A syn elimination through a six-membered cyclic transition state
An E1 path through a carbocation
questions.explain: The five atoms O, N, Cα, Cβ and H form the cyclic transition state, so H and the N-oxide group leave from the same face. The six-membered transition state belongs to ester and xanthate pyrolysis.

questions.q: The N-oxide of N,N-dimethylbutan-2-amine is heated. The major alkene is:
questions.explain: With β-hydrogens on both a CH₃ and a CH₂, the bulky N-oxide removes the more accessible CH₃ hydrogen, giving the less substituted (Hofmann) alkene.

questions.q: An ethyl ester R–C(=O*)–O–CH₂CH₃, with its carbonyl oxygen labelled (O*), is pyrolysed to RCOOH and ethene. Where is the label found?
options: In water released during the reaction
questions.explain: In this Ei syn elimination the carbonyl oxygen abstracts the β-hydrogen through a six-membered cyclic transition state, so O* becomes the –OH of the acid.
